q: The 'Economic Survey 2021-22' was presented on:
explanation: The Economic Survey 2021-22 was presented on 31 January 2022 by the Finance Minister and its theme was 'Time to Move'.

q: The 'Human Development Report 2021-22' used the data of the year:
explanation: The Human Development Report 2021-22 used the 2019 data because of the data gaps created by the Covid pandemic and India was ranked 131st.

q: The 'Environmental Performance Index 2022' placed India at the rank of:
explanation: In the Environmental Performance Index 2022 India was ranked 180th among the 180 countries covered and it scored the lowest in the air quality.

q: The 'Global Gender Gap Report 2022' of the World Economic Forum placed India at:
explanation: In the Global Gender Gap Report 2022 India was ranked 129th and it was the only country in the bottom 150 with a negative score on the health and the education sub-index.

q: The 'SDG India Index 2021-22' was prepared with the help of:
options: The Oxford Policy and Human Development Centre
explanation: The SDG India Index 2021-22 was prepared with the technical assistance of the Oxford Policy and Human Development Centre and it used the district data of 2018-19.

q: The 'India State of Forest Report 2021' reported the forest and tree cover of:
options: 21.76 per cent of the geographical area
explanation: The India State of Forest Report 2021 reported the forest and the tree cover of 21.76 per cent of the geographical area with an increase of 1.89 percentage points over 2019.

q: The 'World Happiness Report 2022' was based on the Gallup World Poll data of:
explanation: The World Happiness Report 2022 used the 2021 Gallup World Poll data and India was ranked 140th.

q: The 'Global Competitiveness' of India in the World Economic Forum's index for 2021-22 was at the rank of:
explanation: In the Global Competitiveness Report 2021-22 India was ranked 56th among the 140 economies and in 2022-23 it was 60th.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Literature for 2021' was awarded to:
explanation: The 2021 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Tanzanian writer Abdulrazak Gurnah and the 2022 prize went to the Jon Fosse.

q: The 'Nobel Peace Prize for 2021' was awarded to:
explanation: The 2021 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the Maria Ressa and the Dmitry Muratov for their fight for the freedom of expression and the 2022 prize went to the Ales Bialiatski and the Memorial.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for 2021' was awarded to:
options: David Card and A. Michael Kremer and Guido Imbens
explanation: The 2021 prize in Economic Sciences went to the David Card, the A. Michael Kremer and the Guido Imbens for their empirical work on the labour market.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Chemistry for 2021' was awarded to:
explanation: The 2021 Chemistry prize was awarded to the Benjamin List and the David MacMillan for the development of the asymmetric organocatalysis.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Physics for 2021' was awarded to:
options: Giorgio Parisi and Klaus Hasselmann and Syukuro Manabe
explanation: The 2021 Physics prize went to the Giorgio Parisi for the theories of the disordered systems and the Klaus Hasselmann and the Syukuro Manabe for the physical modelling of the climate.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for 2021' was awarded to:
options: Harvey Alter and Michael Houghton and Charles Rice
explanation: The 2021 Medicine prize was awarded to the David Julius and the Ardem Patapoutian for the discovery of the receptors for the temperature and the touch.

q: The 'Nobel Prize in Literature for 2020' was awarded to:
explanation: The 2020 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the American poet Louise Glück and the 2019 prize went to the Peter Handke.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the World Food Programme is correct?
options: Abiy Ahmed and the Ales Bialiatski and the Memorial
explanation: The 2020 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme for its work in combatting hunger and for its contribution to the peace and the food security.

q: The 'Abiy Ahmed' won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
explanation: The Abiy Ahmed, the Prime Minister of Ethiopia, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019 for his efforts to build peace and to end the Tigray conflict.

q: The 'World Food Prize 2021' was awarded to:
options: Ramesh Rajasingham and the Green Transformation Foundation
explanation: The 2021 World Food Prize was awarded to the CYMcrare and the Modadugu Gupta for the work in the development of the quality wheat varieties.

q: The 'Jnanpith Award for 2021' was given to:
explanation: The 2021 Jnanpith Award was given to the Nilamani Phookan for his poetry collection in the Assamese language.

q: The 'Sahitya Akademi Award for 2021' in English was given to:
explanation: The Manilal H. Patel won the 2021 Sahitya Akademi Award for English for his collection of short stories Audition.

q: The 'Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2021' was given to:
explanation: The 2021 Dadasaheb Phalke Award was given to the Rajkummar Rao for his contribution to the Indian cinema.

q: The 'Bharat Ratna' awardees of 2021 were:
options: The Pranab Mukherjee and the S. Padmanabhan and the Mulayam Singh and the Charanjit Singh
explanation: The 2021 Bharat Ratna awards went to the Pranab Mukherjee and the S. Padmanabhan and the Mulayam Singh and the Charanjit Singh.

q: Which of the following was among the recipients of the Padma Vibhushan in 2021?
options: the classical vocalist K. S. Nissar Ahmed
explanation: The Padma Vibhushan of 2021 included the classical vocalist K. S. Nissar Ahmed, Tarun Gogoi, R. M. Veerappa, D. K. Pattammal, Shyam Sunder Singh, Kantaben Vora and Ramachandra Guha.

q: The 'Arjuna Award for 2021' was given in the discipline of:
options: Cricket, the athletics, the badminton, the boxing and the chess
explanation: The 2021 Arjuna Awards were announced for the cricket, the athletics, the badminton, the boxing and the chess, among others.

q: The 'Dronacharya Award for 2021' was given to:
options: The B. B. Bhagwat and the S. M. Arif and the Dharmendra and the Sanjay Bhardwaj
explanation: The 2021 Dronacharya Awards were given to the B. B. Bhagwat, the S. M. Arif, the Dharmendra and the Sanjay Bhardwaj.

q: The 'Paris 2024 Olympic' medals of India:
explanation: At the Paris 2024 Games India won one silver in the men's archery individual compound and five bronze medals for a total of six.

q: The 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna' was renamed in:
explanation: The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021 and it is the highest sporting honour in India.

q: The D.G. Gadgil Cup is:
options: the badminton tournament of the Kerala
the Ranji Trophy of the D. G. Gadgil and it is the premier domestic cricket tournament
the football tournament of the Assam
the hockey tournament of the Delhi
explanation: The D. G. Gadgil Cup, the Ranji Trophy, is India's premier domestic cricket championship and it is named after the D. G. Gadgil.

q: The 'Vijay Hazare Trophy' is for:
explanation: The Vijay Hazare Trophy is the first-class cricket tournament of India and the Irani Cup is the one that is played between the Ranji and the Rani of the Services.

q: The Dronacharya Award is:
options: the highest honour for the coaches in the sports
explanation: The Dronacharya Award, instituted in 1985, is the highest national honour for the coaches in the sports.

q: The 'Subroto Cup' is associated with:
explanation: The Subroto Cup is the oldest and the most prestigious international junior football tournament of Asia, instituted in memory of the Subroto Bagchi.

q: The ' Durand Cup' is associated with:
explanation: The Durand Cup, the oldest of the Indian football tournaments, was instituted in 1888 by the Sir Mortimer Durand.

q: The 'Nehru Cup' of the hockey:
options: Is a junior hockey tournament that is also called the Santosh Cup
explanation: The Nehru Cup, the junior hockey tournament of India, is also known as the Santosh Cup.

q: The Vijay Amritraj was:
options: the first Indian tennis player to be ranked in the top ten of the ATP
the first Indian to win a Grand Slam
the first to win the Davis Cup for India
explanation: The Vijay Amritraj was the first Indian tennis player to be ranked in the ATP top ten and he was also the first to be ranked among the world's top eight.

q: The Major Dhyan Chand was:
options: the hockey player who won three consecutive Olympic golds for India in 1928, 1932 and 1936
explanation: The Major Dhyan Chand, the hockey wizard, won the three consecutive Olympic golds for India in 1928, 1932 and 1936 and the Trophy of the Hockey Wizard is named after him.

q: The K. D. Jadhav was:
options: the first Indian Olympic gold medallist in the athletics
he won a gold in the 1928 Olympics
the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold in 1952
explanation: The K. D. Jadhav, the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold, won the gold in the freestyle wrestling in the 1952 Helsinki Games.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Milkha Singh?
options: Milkha Singh was the Flying Sikh and he won the 400 metres at the 1958 Asian Games
explanation: The Milkha Singh, the Flying Sikh, won the 400 metres at the 1958 Asian Games in Tokyo and he was the first Indian to win a Commonwealth individual gold in 1958.

q: The 'P. T. Usha' is:
options: The first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the Asian Track and Field Championships
The first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal
explanation: The P. T. Usha won the 400 metres hurdles gold at the 1986 Asian Track and Field Championships in Seoul and she missed the Olympic medal by a fraction of a second in 1984.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Sita Sahu?
options: The Sita Sahu is the wife of the Deepak and the Amita and the Ayesha are the daughters
explanation: The Sita Sahu, the wife of the Deepak Rao, and their daughters the Amita and the Ayesha are the prominent members of the Indian Idol family of the singers.

q: The Chandrayaan-3 landing was:
options: in August 2023 and the mission cost was about Rs. 450 crore
explanation: The Chandrayaan-3, launched on 14 July 2023, landed on 23 August 2023 at a cost of about Rs. 450 crore, making it the most cost-effective lunar mission.

q: In the context of the Gaganyaan, which of the following is correct?
options: The Gaganyaan is the Indian human spaceflight programme and the four astronaut candidates were selected in 2022
It is the first Indian Mars mission
explanation: The Gaganyaan is the Indian human spaceflight programme, the four astronaut candidates were selected in 2022 and the uncrewed test flight was carried out in 2024.

q: The 'Mangalyaan' was the cheapest Mars mission of the world at about:
explanation: The Mangalyaan cost about Rs. 450 crore, about a tenth of the average of the other Mars missions, and India became the first country to reach Mars on the first attempt.

q: In the context of the Astra, which of the following is correct?
options: It is the hypersonic weapon of the DRDO
The Astra is the new name of the DRDO long range missile and it was test fired in 2023
explanation: The DRDO renamed its long range missile the Astra and it was test fired successfully in August 2023 from the Integrated Test Range in the Odisha.

q: The 'Mission Shakti' of 2019 was:
options: The anti-satellite test that destroyed a satellite in the low earth orbit
explanation: The Mission Shakti of March 2019 was the ASAT test in which the DRDO destroyed the target satellite in the low earth orbit with the Microsat-R.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Axiom-4?
options: The Axiom-4 mission carried the Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla to the International Space Station in 2025
explanation: The Axiom-4 mission of 2025 carried the Shubhanshu Shukla, the second Indian in space, to the International Space Station.

q: The 'Operation Sindoor' of 2025 was:
options: It was a cyclone relief operation
It was a border irrigation project
The military operation to neutralise the terrorist infrastructure in the Pakistan administered Kashmir after the Pahalgam attack
explanation: The Operation Sindoor of May 2025 was the military operation to neutralise the terrorist infrastructure in the Pakistan administered Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the SPADEX?
options: The SPADEX is the Indian space docking experiment planned for the Gaganyaan
explanation: The SPADEX, the Space Docking Experiment, is the Indian plan to demonstrate the autonomous docking capability that the Gaganyaan requires.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Covaxin?
options: It is the mRNA vaccine of the SII
It is a protein subunit vaccine
The Covaxin is the inactivated whole virion vaccine of the Bharat Biotech
explanation: The Covaxin, the inactivated whole virion vaccine against the SARS-CoV-2, was developed by the Bharat Biotech and the Covishield is the viral vector vaccine of the Serum Institute.

q: The 'CoWIN' platform was used for:
options: The covid vaccination registration and the certificates
explanation: The CoWIN, the Co-Win Information Network, was the digital platform of the covid vaccination drive, the largest of its kind in the world.

q: The 'IndiaAI Mission' was approved with an outlay of:
explanation: The IndiaAI Mission was approved in March 2024 with a fiscal outlay of about Rs. 10,372 crore for the compute, the datasets, the applications and the innovation.

q: The 'National Quantum Mission' was approved in 2023 with an outlay of:
explanation: The National Quantum Mission, approved in 2023, has an outlay of Rs. 6,003.25 crore for the quantum computers, the communication and the sensing technologies.

q: The 'first Indian semiconductor fab' at the Sanand:
options: Was approved in 2022 under the India Semiconductor Mission and the Micron is the partner
It is in the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Micron's semiconductor fabrication unit at the Sanand in the Gujarat was approved in 2022 with the support of about Rs. 30,000 crore of the modified semiconductor programme.

q: Paris Agreement was:
options: adopted in 2015 and it aims to hold the temperature rise well below 2 degrees C above the pre-industrial level
explanation: The Paris Agreement, adopted in December 2015, aims to hold the increase of the global average temperature well below 2 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial level.

q: Completed the first Global Stocktake and called:
options: Completed the first Global Stocktake and called for the transition away from the fossil fuels
Was the COP that agreed the Loss and Damage Fund
Was the COP that created the NDC
explanation: The COP28 at the Dubai in December 2023 completed the first Global Stocktake and it called for the transition away from the fossil fuels in the energy systems.

q: The 'COP29' in the Baku in 2024 agreed:
options: A new collective quantified goal of at least USD 300 billion a year by 2035 for the climate finance
explanation: The COP29 in the Baku in November 2024 agreed the new collective quantified goal of at least USD 300 billion a year by 2035 for the developing countries.

q: The 'Loss and Damage Fund' was agreed at the:
explanation: The Loss and Damage Fund for the developing countries was agreed at the COP27 in the Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022 and it was operationalised at the COP28.

q: The 'Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework' was adopted in:
options: December 2022 at the COP15 of the CBD
explanation: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at the COP15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity in December 2022 with the target of protecting the 30 per cent of the land and the sea by 2030.

q: The 'BBNJ Agreement' on the high seas was adopted in:
explanation: The Agreement on the Marine Biodiversity of the Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction was adopted in June 2023 to establish the marine protected areas in the high seas.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the PM-Kusum is correct?
options: Is the rooftop solar scheme for the households
Is the scheme of the solar pumps, the solar power plants and the solarisation of the farms
explanation: The PM-KUSUM has the three components of the solar power for the farm pumps, the solar power plants of the 10,000 units and the solarisation of the grid-connected small rural plants.

q: The 'E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022' came into force on:
explanation: The E-waste (Management) Rules of 2022 came into force on 1 April 2023 and they extended the producer responsibility to the twenty-one categories of the electrical and the electronic equipment.

q: The 'Single-use plastic ban' came into effect in India on:
explanation: The ban on the identified single-use plastic items came into effect on 1 July 2022 and the plastic waste management rules of 2016 had banned them earlier.

q: The 'National Mission on Natural Farming' was launched in:
explanation: The National Mission on Natural Farming was launched in 2023 with the objective of the promotion in about 10 lakh hectares across the 2,800 blocks of the country.
